questions.question: A select mortality model records selection age and duration since selection. Its select period is three years. Two lives are both aged 42: one was selected at 40 and the other at 41. What does the model permit for their death probabilities over the next year?
options: Their rates must agree because their attained ages agree.
Their rates must agree because both have survived selection.
Their rates may differ because their selection histories differ.
Both rates must already be ultimate because both lives are older than 40.

questions.question: In a select model, $q_{[x]+s}$ denotes next-year death probability for selection age $x$ and elapsed duration $s$. A life was selected at age 35 and is now aged 37. Which notation describes its current next-year death probability?

A select model has select period $r=2$ years. Write $q_{[x]+s}$ for next-year death probability at duration $s$ after selection at age $x$, and $q_y$ for the ultimate rate at attained age $y$. A life selected at 50 has just reached age 52. Which prescribed rate now applies?
options: $q_{[52]}$, the new-selection rate at age 52.
$q_{51}$, the ultimate rate in the preceding year.
A separate select rate until duration 3, then $q_{53}$.

questions.question: A mortality model assumes that selection effects disappear after three years, so rates then depend only on attained age. What does this assumption establish about real insured populations?
options: It proves that every real population has no selection effect after three years.
It specifies the model, without proving that real selection effects end then.
It proves that underwriting has no effect during the first three years either.
It proves that all attained ages have equal mortality after three years.

questions.question: At an attained age inside a two-year select period, a model gives newly selected lives annual death probability 0.03 and the ultimate table gives 0.02 at that same age. Which assessment follows from the definition of a select model alone?
options: The select rate must be replaced by 0.02 because attained age fixes mortality.
The rates are invalid because selection must strictly lower mortality.
The rates are permitted; selection need not lower mortality in every model.
The select period must be shortened to zero whenever the select rate is larger.

questions.question: A life selected at age 50 has annual death probabilities $q_{[50]}=0.1$ and $q_{[50]+1}=0.2$. What is the probability, measured at selection, of dying during the second year?

A select model has period $r=3$ years. A life selected at age 50 is observed four years later. Ultimate annual death rates are $q_{50}=0.01$, $q_{53}=0.02$ and $q_{54}=0.025$. Which rate applies over its next year?
options: A new select rate at age 54 is needed.

questions.question: A mortality model sets its select period to $r=0$. Write $q_{[x]+s}$ for death probability at integer duration $s\geq0$ after selection at $x$, and $q_y$ for the ultimate death probability at attained age $y$. Which consequence is required for all such ages and durations?
options: $q_{[x]}$ may differ from $q_x$, but all later durations are ultimate.
$q_{[x]+s}=q_x$ at every duration because selection ends immediately.
$q_{[x]+s}=0$ because no select years remain.
$q_{[x]+s}=q_{x+s}$ from the selection date onwards.

questions.question: A life selected at age 40 has a two-year select period, with annual death rates $q_{[40]}=0.005$ and $q_{[40]+1}=0.007$. At attained age 42 the ultimate annual rate is $q_{42}=0.01$. What is three-year survival from selection?

At attained age 50, a portfolio currently contains 300 recently selected lives with next-year death probability 0.02 and 700 ultimate lives with next-year death probability 0.04. A life is chosen uniformly from these 1000 current survivors. What is its next-year death probability?

A model has select period $r=3$. For a life selected at 40, its duration-1 annual death rate equals the ultimate age-41 rate, both 0.02. At duration 2 its select rate is 0.04 while the ultimate age-42 rate is 0.03. An analyst declares that the effective ultimate period began at duration 1 because the rates matched then. Which assessment is correct?
options: The declared switch is valid because one equal pair proves history no longer matters.
The model contradicts r=3 because select and ultimate rates must differ before r.
One matching interval does not establish a permanent ultimate switch.
The select period must be increased to four because the duration-2 rates differ.

questions.question: A two-year select model compares two surviving groups currently aged 42. Group A was selected at 40 and has cumulative survival 0.95 since selection; group B was selected at 39 and has cumulative survival 0.90 since selection. The common ultimate next-year death rate at age 42 is 0.02. Which statement is justified?
options: Both current next-year rates and cumulative survivals must agree because both groups are ultimate.
Their current next-year rates must be 0.05 and 0.10, the complements of their cumulative survivals.
Only group B is ultimate, since group A has reached exactly two years.
Both current next-year rates are 0.02, while their stated cumulative survivals differ.

questions.question: A model specifies a two-year select period. Two survivor cohorts are currently aged 42: A was selected at 40 and B at 39. Over the next year A decreases from 1000 to 980 and B from 800 to 776. If these counts are exact model survivor counts, can both belong to this model with a common ultimate table?
options: Yes: different original selection ages permit different rates at every duration.
No: their ultimate age-42 annual death rates would be 0.02 and 0.03.
Yes: the different current cohort sizes account for the different annual rates.
No: a common ultimate rate requires equal death counts in both cohorts.

questions.question: A life selected at age 40 has already survived one year. Its model has a two-year select period and annual death rates $q_{[40]}=0.1$, $q_{[40]+1}=0.2$, and ultimate $q_{42}=0.3$. Assuming positive probability of that first-year survival, what is its conditional probability of surviving the next two years from its current age 41?
